title: ICE Just Suspended Vehicle Stops Nationwide. For Millions of Immigrants, the Relief May Be Temporary.
excerpt: Two fatal shootings in six days forced the agency's hand. Immigration advocates say the policy should have never existed.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • ICE has suspended vehicle stops for immigration enforcement nationwide after two fatal shootings.
  • The suspension affects ICE's primary method of arresting immigrants, requiring warrants for home entries.
  • At least seven people have died during immigration enforcement since January 2025.
  • Protests erupted in Biddeford, Maine, following the recent shootings, raising questions about ICE's practices.
  • The suspension provides temporary relief for Indian immigrants amid a hostile enforcement environment.
Impact of ICE's Vehicle Stop Suspension
›ICE's daily arrest target: 2,000
›Fatal shootings: 2 in 6 days
›Total deaths since January 2025: 7
›Maine ICE arrests increased to 70 per day in July
Immigration and Customs Enforcement has suspended vehicle stops for immigration enforcement across the entire United States, two sources briefed on the matter told Reuters on Tuesday — a sharp reversal for an agency that had been ramping up arrests to meet a quota of 2,000 per day. The decision came one day after an ICE officer fatally shot Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man authorized to work in the United States, during a traffic stop in Biddeford, Maine. Guerrero was not the intended target of the operation. He was leaving a residence that agents had been surveilling when officers tried to pull over his vehicle. The Department of Homeland Security said the officer fired because he was "fearing for public safety," but officials did not explain what threat the driver posed. Six days earlier, a separate ICE traffic stop in Houston ended with agents fatally shooting 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national. DHS initially said Salgado Araujo had "weaponized" his vehicle and tried to run over an officer. Witnesses in the van disputed that account. ## A Key Enforcement Tool, Gone Overnight > **"DHS initially said Salgado Araujo had "weaponized" his vehicle and tried to run over an officer."** The suspension eliminates one of ICE's most relied-upon arrest methods. In recent weeks, officers had been staking out the homes and workplaces of immigrants targeted for arrest, most often catching them as they left by car. Without vehicle stops, agents will increasingly need to enter suspects' homes — which requires a search warrant signed off by a judge, a significantly higher legal bar. "Numbers are going down, we can't do s–t," an ICE source told the Daily Wire, referring to the immediate impact on arrest figures. The exception: agents with a criminal warrant can still initiate a vehicle stop, but only in coordination with other law enforcement agencies. For routine immigration enforcement, the tool is effectively off the table. Maine Senator Susan Collins, a Republican, said she urged DHS Secretary to cease non-urgent stops after the Biddeford shooting raised "critical questions." Senator Angus King, an independent who caucuses with Democrats, noted that the agents involved were not wearing body cameras — leaving a significant gap in the evidentiary record. ## Seven Dead Since January 2025 The two shootings bring the total number of people killed during immigration enforcement operations to at least seven since President Trump returned to office in January 2025 and launched his mass deportation campaign. In Maine alone, ICE arrests have more than quadrupled since the beginning of June, climbing to around 70 per day in early July, according to internal ICE data shared with Reuters. The surge reflects the administration's broader push to hit its daily arrest targets, which has meant officers are being deployed more aggressively and with less oversight than in previous administrations.
Fatal Shootings Raise Concerns
July 2023
ICE officer fatally shoots Joan Sebastian Guerrero during a traffic stop.
July 2023
ICE officer fatally shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston.
July 2023
ICE suspends vehicle stops nationwide.
Multiple protests erupted in Biddeford on Monday, with further demonstrations scheduled for Tuesday across Maine. The shooting has intensified a national debate over whether ICE agents — who are not trained as traditional law enforcement officers — should be making traffic stops at all. ## What This Means for the Indian Diaspora For Indian immigrants in the United States — including an estimated 725,000 undocumented individuals and hundreds of thousands more on temporary work visas — the suspension offers a moment of relief in an otherwise hostile enforcement environment. The Vance-led H-1B fraud investigation announced last week already rattled the Indian professional community. Taken together, these developments paint a picture of an immigration enforcement apparatus under enormous strain: expanding its reach faster than its training, oversight, or legal authority can support. The suspension is described as immediate but its duration is unclear. ICE declined to comment on the specific policy change, saying only: "We are always evaluating our procedures to keep our officers safe and criminals off our streets." For the families of Joan Sebastian Guerrero and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the evaluation came too late.

nri_angle: Indian immigrants in the US — both undocumented and on temporary visas — face reduced risk of traffic stop encounters, but the suspension's duration is uncertain amid a broader crackdown.
